engineered_columns_excluded: all lag/roll/rain_*_d/neighbour/up_* columns (E13 keeps raw-vs-engineered interpretable)
fitted_statistics: none - raw calendar scatter + windowing only

window.definition: X[i,k,:] = station row at day (date_i - L + 1 + k); window ends ON the anchor day
window.front_pad: NaN before the station's first calendar day
window.gap_policy: absent calendar days are all-NaN timesteps (policy chosen in Phase 19)

missing_timestep_policy.name: keep-all + observation mask channel
missing_timestep_policy.statement: No timestep and no sample is dropped or imputed. Every window keeps all L timesteps. A timestep whose calendar day is absent from the model table is written to the tensor as all-NaN in Dataset B and handed to the model as mask=0 (binary mask channel, sequence_mask_L{L}.npy); observed days are mask=1. On present days the ~0.1% variable-level NaNs (precip_mm, tmax_c, tmin_c) are replaced by 0 AFTER the training fold's standardisation, i.e. by the fold mean - no information, no fitting outside the fold. Phase 21 input is therefore concat(12 raw variables, mask) = 13 channels; a plain NaN must never reach a layer.
why: identical sample sets for L = 3/7/14/30 - the D12 length sweep stays comparable (rejection would train different models on different data)
nothing is fabricated: interpolation/forward-fill would invent driver variables (precip_mm), age-2 filling (R4) still drops samples
the cheapest rejected alternative (R2) drops 2.9-26.7% of samples, L-dependent and distribution-shifting (S3b)
